chunks: As for what ʿAbd Allah ibn Muskan narrated from Layth al-Muradi, he said:

I asked Aba ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about salat in the summer, during the short nights—salat al-layl in the first part of the night. He said: Yes, excellent is what you considered, and excellent is what you did.

So this report bears two possibilities: one of them is that it is a concession for the traveler, and the second is that it is a concession for one upon whom standing in the latter part of the night is difficult and who is not able to make it up. Then it is permissible for him in that case to advance it to the first part of the night. This is indicated by that.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat, the ritual prayer being discussed here
key_terms.اللَّيَالِي الْقِصَارِ: short nights, especially relevant in summer timing
key_terms.الْقَضَاءِ: making up an act of worship after its time
key_terms.الْقِيَامُ: rising or standing for worship at night
key_terms.الْمُسَافِرِ: the traveler, for whom the concession may apply
key_terms.تَقْدِيمُهَا: performing it earlier than its usual time
key_terms.صَلَاةِ اللَّيْلِ: the night prayer performed during the night hours

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform Salat al-Layl at the beginning of the night in summer or when rising later is difficult?
ai.summary: This report discusses the permissibility of performing Salat al-Layl in the first part of the night during summer when the nights are short. It indicates a legal concession, especially for a traveler or for someone who finds it difficult to rise at the end of the night and cannot perform it later as qada'.
